records.surface: Endpoint owner: a 5-of-9 LayerZero multisig that sets default libraries
records.summary_short: A 5-of-9 LayerZero multisig sets the defaults; the docs say defaults may change
records.onchain_observed: EndpointV2 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c: owner() = OneSig 0xBe010A7e3686FdF65E93344ab664D065A0B02478 (threshold() = 5 of totalSigners() = 9), which registers message libraries and sets default libraries and configurations without a timelock; the Base endpoint owner is OneSig 0xa0392d116D71ED3b75086194aBa6De3CD1e39B7E (5 of 9, the same signers).
records.documented_reference: docs.layerzero.network (defaults): 'You should always set your DVN configuration explicitly. Defaults are placeholder configurations — they may be Dead DVNs that prevent message delivery, may include only a single DVN, and may change without notice.' / 'This default configuration can vary per channel, changing the placeholder block confirmations, the X‑of‑Y‑of‑N thresholds for verification, the Executor, and the message libraries.' / 'Once an application defines its channel’s X‑of‑Y‑of‑N security settings, those parameters are enforced at the protocol level indefinitely. Only the application delegate can update these configurations. There is no governance, upgrade mechanism, or external actor that can alter or disable a channel’s configuration once set, guaranteeing that security guarantees persist without relying on LayerZero.'

records.surface: Messages need 13 of the 19 guardians (guardian set 7)
records.summary_short: Ethereum core contract needs 13 of 19 guardian signatures, as documented
records.onchain_observed: Wormhole core 0x98f3c9e6E3fAce36bAAd05FE09d375Ef1464288B: getCurrentGuardianSetIndex() = 7; getGuardianSet(7) = 19 keys, expirationTime 0; quorum(19) = 13.
records.documented_reference: wormhole.com/docs (guardians / security): 'Once a sufficient delegate quorum is reached or once Guardians independently observe the event, signatures accumulate until the required 13-of-19 quorum is achieved.' / 'Some chains (such as Ethereum and Solana) are secured by all 19 Guardians.' / 'The Core Contract does not distinguish between chains with direct observation and delegated chains; it verifies only that a valid 13-of-19 VAA has been produced.'

records.surface: Message fee: 0 (publishing is free)

records.documented_reference: wormhole.com/docs (core contracts): 'There are no fees to publish a message except when publishing on Solana, but this is subject to change in the future.'

records.surface: Upgrades: guardian-signed governance messages only, no admin key
records.summary_short: Core contract upgrades need 13 of 19 guardians signing a governance message, as documented
records.onchain_observed: Wormhole core 0x98f3c9e6E3fAce36bAAd05FE09d375Ef1464288B: EIP-1967 implementation = 0x3c3d457f1522D3540AB3325Aa5f1864E34cBA9D0; EIP-1967 admin slot = 0x0 (no proxy admin); governanceChainId() = 1, governanceContract() = 0x04; upgrades only through submitContractUpgrade with a governance message signed by the current guardian set's quorum.
records.documented_reference: wormhole.com/docs (governance / security): 'Governance is the process through which contract upgrades happen. Guardians manually vote on governance proposals that originate inside the Guardian Network and are then submitted to ecosystem contracts.' / 'This means that governance actions are held to the same security standard as the rest of the system. A two-thirds supermajority of the Guardians is required to pass any governance action.' / 'Governance messages can target any of the various wormhole modules, including the core contracts and all currently deployed Wrapped Token Transfers (WTT) contracts. When a Guardian signs such a message, its signature implies a vote on the action in question. Once more than two-thirds of the Guardians have signed, the message and governance action are considered valid.'
